title: Desktop: button hitboxes misalign when window shrinks (desktop and mobile)
description: When the desktop page is narrowed, or opened on a phone, clickable areas no longer line up with the drawn buttons. Which screens and by how much is not yet recorded. Suspects found by reading code (none reproduced): (1) Tuner canvas is a fixed 960x540 CSS box in v2/src/desktop/TunerScreen.ts and the controls row never wraps, so content overflows and body overflow:hidden clips it. (2) canvas {100vw/100vh} and #screen-container {fixed; inset:0} in v2/desktop.html disagree on mobile where 100vh includes browser chrome, switch to dvh or inset-based sizing. (3) TunerScreen reads devicePixelRatio once at mount, so browser zoom or moving between monitors changes DPR without a canvas rescale. (4) #active-overlay fades to opacity 0.12 on idle but .active-bar stays pointer-events:auto, and the reveal listens to mousemove only, so touch never un-fades it. (5) Fixed-px layouts: settings panel min-width 340px, pre-tune/pre-play aspect-ratio buttons. Next step: reproduce at ~400px wide, inspect with devtools element outlines per screen (Library, PreScene, ActiveScene, Tuner, Settings), then narrow the cause.
acceptance_criteria: Repro steps recorded per affected screen, root cause identified, buttons clickable exactly where drawn at widths down to 360px on desktop and on a phone.

title: XR: gate note scoring and re-tune on whether the user tuned (design, undecided)
description:
NO DECISION MADE. This records the 2026-10-18 discussion so it can be settled later.

Context: XR Play no longer auto-opens the tuner (only a USB mic works reliably, so tuning is optional via the Song page Tune button, see RockyRoad-0q4.5). XR Play also has no PitchDetector or NoteDetector, so it never says whether notes are right. Most XR users will not tune, so they should not get right/wrong feedback. Users who did tune could get it, and could be re-tuned automatically when they open a song with different tuningOffsets.

Idea under discussion:
- Scoring needs a working mic and the tuner is the only place XR confirms one, so "has tuned" is a proxy for "can be scored".
- Re-tune only matters when scoring is on. It would be a consequence (scoring on and the part's tuningOffsets differ from the last completed tuning, desktop's lastTuningKey rule) rather than its own setting.

Options considered:
- Two layers: derived capability (tuned this session, in memory, not shown) plus one persisted xrScoring preference (default off, in Settings). Tuning never changes the preference, so nothing flips a visible setting behind the user's back.
- One bool: completing the first tune turns xrScoring on once, then the user owns it (needs a hidden "seen" flag).
- Rejected as odd: auto-flipping a visible scoring toggle every time a tune completes.

Open questions:
- Is the toggle a Settings item or a Song page choice next to Tune?
- Is "tuned" session-only (matches desktop, but the Quest browser reloads often) or persisted?
- With scoring off, hide the right/wrong feedback UI entirely or just stop updating it?

Dependencies and caveats:
- Needs note detection in XR Play (NoteDetector plus a per-frame PitchDetector.detect(), as desktop ActiveSceneScreen does). That is not built and may be its own bead.
- The tuner's chosen input device is not persisted (XRTunerScene._inputId). Scoring in Play would fall back to the weak built-in mic, so the USB device must be remembered, with a fallback when its deviceId is gone.
- Once scoring exists, handing the tuner's live detector into Play avoids a second mic request.
- Guitar and bass only. Keys keep today's behavior.

title: Design: shared web design system package across RockyRoad, RockyRoadImport and Aurora
description: Design tokens and web components are hand-copied across 4 consumers (RockyRoad desktop, RockyRoad XR, RockyRoadImport, Aurora) and drift. Examples: Aurora tokens.css copies XR panel.css colors, Aurora Dropdown.js is a port of src/desktop/Dropdown.ts that gained ARIA work never ported back (6zf), desktop buttons drifted per screen (4bi.5). Decide whether and how to share. Scope: web only (tokens, CSS components like .btn/toggle/slider/dropdown, plain JS/TS Dropdown logic). Not shareable: XR uikitml (unitless world-space sizing, only color values carry over) and desktop px sizes vs XR sizes. Decisions needed: (1) host repo and source of truth, (2) packaging: npm workspace, git submodule, or vendored copy with sync script (Aurora already vendors under demo/vendor/webui with MANIFEST.json), (3) first slice, likely tokens + buttons, (4) whether XR consumes generated color values. Sequence after 4bi.5 and 6zf land so the package starts from a consolidated baseline. If adopted, the RockyRoadImport ARIA port becomes 'adopt shared Dropdown' rather than a separate port bead.
acceptance_criteria: Written decision (host, packaging mechanism, first slice, XR color strategy) and follow-up beads filed for the first slice and each consumer's adoption.
